reports.title: Kimberly-Clark Announces Third Quarter Results, Reaffirms 2026 Standalone Outlook

guidance.heading: 2026 Outlook
section: The company continues to expect 2026 Organic Sales Growth to be approximately 100 basis points below its weighted average category growth in the categories and countries it competes, which is approximately 1.7 percent on a trailing twelve-month basis. This primarily reflects realized and potential unfavorable impacts amounting to approximately 100 basis points at a total company level from the previously disclosed China social media disruptions. Adjusted Operating Profit is expected to grow mid-single digits on a constant-currency basis. Adjusted Earnings Per Share from Continuing Operations are expected to grow high single digits on a constant-currency basis. Adjusted Earnings Per Share Attributable to Kimberly-Clark are expected to see a low single digit decline on a constant-currency basis.
This outlook reflects assumptions subject to change given the macro environment.

desk.headline: Sales flat at $4.13bn, slight miss; adjusted EPS $1.70 beat; 2026 standalone outlook reaffirmed as Kenvue deal closes
results: Net sales slipped 0.4% to $4.13bn and organic sales fell 1.3%, hurt by a social-media-driven disruption in China and retailer stock cuts in North America.
Adjusted EPS from continuing operations rose 17% to $1.70, but mainly on lower interest costs and a lower tax rate; adjusted operating profit dipped 0.9%.
Adjusted gross margin fell 1.3 points to 35.5% as prices lagged cost inflation; North America profit rose 2.7% while International Personal Care profit fell 33%.
Total EPS of $5.37 includes a $1.4bn gain from moving its International Family Care and Professional business into the Arbex joint venture with Suzano.
Nine-month operating cash flow rose to $2.4bn and $1.3bn was paid in dividends; the Kenvue acquisition closed on 2 November.

guidance.summary: Kimberly-Clark kept its 2026 outlook for the business before Kenvue: organic growth about 1 point below its categories, adjusted operating profit up mid-single digits and adjusted EPS from continuing operations up high-single digits (constant currency).

points: Management called the Kenvue deal a defining milestone and repeated a target of about $1.9bn of cost savings from combining the two.
For 2027, the combined company expects adjusted earnings dilution of no more than mid-single digits versus standalone, improving through 2028.
China authorities confirmed Huggies' product safety, but rebuilding consumer trust will need sustained investment.
Full-year cost inflation of about $250m, mostly in the second half and driven by North American freight, is being offset by productivity.
call.source: Call coverage: Zacks via Yahoo Finance, 6 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)
